findings.location: Proof, step 5.1, construction and normalization of the bump on each tree-edge overlap
findings.evidence: The step chooses and normalizes a nonnegative smooth bump on each open overlap, but the item only supplies Heine–Borel and neither proves bump existence nor finite positive integral. Add the smooth-bump lemma using a ball contained in the overlap, and establish the bump integral is finite and positive before normalizing.

findings.location: Facts & Assumptions F9 and Proof, step 2.1
findings.evidence: The proof applies the L1 approximate-identity convergence theorem to rescalings of the selected unit-mass kernel, but neither F9 nor the dependencies show that these rescalings form an L1 approximate identity. Add prop-mollifier-families-are-l-one-approximate-identities or verify mass one, uniform L1 norm, and shrinking support for this family.

findings.location: Facts & Assumptions F2 and Proof, step 1.1, local application on each cover patch
findings.evidence: The local star-shaped Bogovskii theorem requires a nonnegative unit-mass kernel supported in the patch’s star-shaped ball. The bounded-domain proof invokes that theorem on each patch but never chooses or constructs the required kernel from the cover. Choose and normalize a smooth bump in each supplied ball, or make the cover provide those kernels.
